method: OPEN AND QUOTED from Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360) 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma' (published 4 November 2024). Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC11570806).

claims.claim: **RAI-refractory DTC affects under 5% of patients but has a 10-year survival of only 10%**, so early recognition matters.
claims.source_text: there is a subset of patients (<5%) who develop RAI-resistant or -refractory differentiated thyroid carcinoma (RAIRTC) … RAIRTC has a dismal prognosis among all follicular cell-derived differentiated thyroid cancer types, with a 10-year survival rate of only 10%
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360), 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma', published 4 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11570806/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The five defining scenarios:** metastases progressing despite RAI uptake; no uptake on the post-therapy scan despite known structural disease; uptake in some foci but not others; progression after a cumulative RAI activity above 22.2 GBq (600 mCi); and no uptake on a diagnostic radioiodine scan.
claims.source_text: defined RAIRTC by outlining five key clinical scenarios indicative of disease: progression of thyroid cancer metastases despite RAI uptake; no RAI uptake in post-therapy scan despite known structural recurrent/metastatic disease; RAI uptake in some but not all cancer foci; thyroid cancer metastases progression despite cumulative RAI activity of >22.2 GBq (600 mCi); and no RAI uptake on diagnostic radioiodine scan
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360), 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma', published 4 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11570806/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Raised thyroglobulin with a negative whole-body scan is a warning:** about a quarter of such patients are scan-negative, because refractory disease does not take up 131I. FDG uptake rises as radioiodine avidity falls.
claims.source_text: approximately one quarter of these patients have negative radioiodine whole-body scans (WBS) (). Indeed, RAIRTC does not concentrate 131I and is therefore unable to be diagnosed/detected via radioiodine WBS. … there is an inverse relationship between the ability to concentrate radioiodine and the uptake of 18F-FDG
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360), 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma', published 4 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11570806/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **FDG-PET is a complementary, case-by-case test**, most useful when structural imaging and clinical suspicion disagree (for example a rising thyroglobulin with no visible disease).
claims.source_text: Our group considers FDG-PET a complementary test, used on a case-by-case basis, for RAIRTC diagnosis and staging, with heterogeneity in terms of timing of when it should be used. While especially valuable in cases of discordance between structural imaging and clinical suspicion … discordance between biochemical parameters and structural imaging (e.g. rising thyroglobulin levels in the absence of anatomical disease measured by standard cross-sectional imaging
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360), 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma', published 4 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11570806/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Histology that predicts poor RAI uptake:** poorly differentiated carcinoma (necrosis and/or at least 3 mitoses per 2 mm2) and high-grade DTC (necrosis and/or at least 5 mitoses per 2 mm2).
claims.source_text: PDTC is defined as an invasive follicular cell-derived non-anaplastic thyroid carcinoma with solid/trabecular/insular growth that is unassociated with nuclear alterations of papillary thyroid carcinomas and that shows tumor necrosis and/or mitotic count of at least 3 mitoses per 2 mm2 … High-grade DTCs are defined by the presence of tumor necrosis and/or mitotic count of at least 5 per 2 mm2 … Similar to PDTCs, high-grade DTCs are also less likely to concentrate RAI
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360), 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma', published 4 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11570806/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **True refractoriness must be proven by giving RAI**, which is also needed to qualify for systemic treatment; other features only raise the suspicion.
claims.source_text: We acknowledge that true RAI refractoriness must ultimately be confirmed by attempting RAI therapy (and to qualify for systemic treatment)
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360), 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma', published 4 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11570806/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refer for local or systemic therapy when there is structural progression despite RAI (highest priority)**; err on the side of referring early, and fast-track patients with heavy disease burden or risk of complications.
claims.source_text: While those with structural disease progression despite RAI therapy are of highest priority, we also suggest scenarios that could be considered for referral, at the physician's discretion. … it will benefit patients to err on the side of caution and refer too soon rather than too late. We also note that patients with a high burden of disease and those at risk of complications should be fast-tracked for an expedited referral where possible.
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360), 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma', published 4 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11570806/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Test tumour tissue early when refractory disease is suspected** (for example FDG-PET positive), rather than waiting until it is proven.
claims.source_text: we recommend earlier use of molecular testing when such features are present in patients with potential RAIRTC to help optimize care.
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360), 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma', published 4 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11570806/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **BRAF mutations, RET fusions and NTRK1-3 fusions must be tested** to establish eligibility for targeted drugs; BRAF V600E immunohistochemistry is an acceptable screen only if rigorously validated and fast.
claims.source_text: BRAF mutations, RET fusions, and NTRK1-3 fusions are essential to measure to determine eligibility for targeted therapies. … BRAF p.V600E-specific immunohistochemistry is therefore recommended as a potential screening tool, if rigorously validated using molecularly characterized cases and available with rapid turnaround.
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360), 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma', published 4 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11570806/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Re-operation carries real morbidity:** transient hypoparathyroidism 7.1%, permanent 2.7%, and recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy 1.6%.
claims.source_text: Repeat resections in patients with potential RAIRTC must be approached cautiously, as re-operative thyroid surgery has been shown to have high rates of post-operative morbidity, including both transient (7.1%) and permanent (2.7%) hypoparathyroidism, and iatrogenic unilateral recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) palsy (1.6%)
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360), 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma', published 4 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11570806/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Small-volume neck disease in an operated field can be watched** if nodes are not enlarging and cytology is not aggressive. Re-operate for oligometastatic, rapidly progressive or symptomatic disease, new neck metastases, or disease threatening major structures.
claims.source_text: Active surveillance may be considered, instead of re-operation, in those with small volume neck disease in a previously operated field. These patients should not have progressively enlarging metastatic lymph nodes or aggressive cytological features … Patients who should be considered for re-operation include those with oligometastatic, rapidly progressive or symptomatic disease, newly discovered metastatic disease in the neck or where recurrent disease is considered to potentially threaten major structures
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360), 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma', published 4 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11570806/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **External beam radiotherapy** does not improve survival or distant spread but does improve locoregional control; use it in selected cases.
claims.source_text: Published studies of EBRT for DTC do not support improved overall survival or rates of distant metastases (). However, there is evidence that EBRT improves locoregional control with acceptable toxicity, especially with use of modern precision radiation therapy technologies (, -). Consistent with published guidelines, we recommend EBRT in select cases for locoregional control
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360), 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma', published 4 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11570806/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Offer SRS/SRT for limited brain metastases** after neurosurgical review, and SABR for oligometastases; phase II data favour SABR in selected patients with up to 5 metastases.
claims.source_text: we recommend SRS/SRT be offered to eligible patients with limited central nervous system metastases after appropriate neurosurgical consultation … we recommend SABR for treatment of oligometastases (extra-cranial, bony, or soft-tissue) … Phase II studies show favorable progression-free survival and local control were observed after SABR in select patients with up to 5 metastases
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360), 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma', published 4 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11570806/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat metastatic disease actively**, especially in younger or fit patients, because it usually progresses slowly.
claims.source_text: Therefore, aggressive management of patients who progress to M1 thyroid cancer, including those with high-risk or RAIRTC, is indicated, especially in those who are younger or have a good performance status
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360), 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma', published 4 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11570806/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Unresectable DTC (under 10% of advanced cases):** neoadjuvant TKI treatment can shrink tumour and reduce surgical morbidity.
claims.source_text: Unresectable DTC occurs in <10% of advanced DTC … TKis have recently been reported to have a role in neoadjuvant treatment of unresectable or locally advanced DTC to reduce tumor volume and surgical morbidity
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360), 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma', published 4 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11570806/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Multikinase inhibitors (lenvatinib, sorafenib, cabozantinib) are indicated for RAI-refractory DTC but are toxic.** In SELECT about 76% had grade 3+ treatment-related events on lenvatinib and 14.2% stopped for adverse events (2.3% on placebo); hypertension, diarrhoea and fatigue were commonest.
claims.source_text: While VEGFR-targeting multikinase inhibitors lenvatinib, sorafenib, and cabozantinib are currently indicated for systemic treatment of RAIRTC, they can be associated with considerable adverse effects. In the SELECT trial of lenvatinib, ~76% of patients experienced grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events, with 14.2% of patients discontinuing the study drug due to adverse events compared to 2.3% with placebo (). The most common adverse effects associated with lenvatinib were hypertension, diarrhea, and fatigue/asthenia
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360), 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma', published 4 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11570806/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **With an actionable alteration, consider a targeted drug.** RET- and NTRK-fusion inhibitors can be used before lenvatinib; BRAF inhibitors should not routinely precede lenvatinib because they are less effective and the evidence is weaker.
claims.source_text: we recommend patients with confirmed, clinically actionable genomic alterations be considered for targeted therapy. While the response rates for NTRK and RET fusion-targeting therapies appear to be promising, supporting their use before lenvatinib in eligible patients, we would not recommend routine use of BRAF inhibitors before lenvatinib, given their lower efficacy and weaker evidence.
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360), 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma', published 4 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11570806/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Immune checkpoint inhibitors only when nothing else is available** and the patient is eligible (e.g. mismatch-repair deficient); pembrolizumab gave a response rate of about 7% in KEYNOTE-158.
claims.source_text: In the Phase 2 KEYNOTE-158 study, pembrolizumab was found to be effective (~7% overall response rate) for a small subset of patients with advanced DTC, regardless of tumor PD-L1 status, with manageable toxicities … we recommend immune checkpoint inhibitors if no other treatments are available and patients are eligible (e.g. DNA mismatch repair deficient
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360), 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma', published 4 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11570806/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cytotoxic chemotherapy is a last resort:** doxorubicin-based regimens give responses of around 20%.
claims.source_text: Chemotherapy (i.e., doxorubicin alone and in combination with other cytotoxic therapy, such as cisplatin) for patients with RAIRTC is generally considered ineffective, with response rates of ~20% … chemotherapy should be considered as a last resort
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360), 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma', published 4 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11570806/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **RAI resensitisation (for example BRAF/MEK inhibition) only within a clinical trial**; adding selumetinib to adjuvant RAI did not improve complete remission in a phase 3 trial.
claims.source_text: a recent Phase 3 trial showed the addition of selumetinib to adjuvant RAI did not significantly improve 18-month complete remission (CR) rate versus placebo plus RAI in patients with DTC at high risk of primary treatment failure … we recommend resensitization only be attempted as part of a clinical trial, with careful monitoring.
claims.locator: Canadian multidisciplinary consensus panel, Frontiers in Oncology 14:1437360 (doi 10.3389/fonc.2024.1437360), 'Multidisciplinary Canadian consensus on the multimodal management of high-risk and radioactive iodine-refractory thyroid carcinoma', published 4 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11570806/, retrieved 2026-09-23
